                                              I.      INTRODUCTION

        1.       V2 Landowners adamantly oppose this 765-kV electric transmission line being

routed through any part of the pristine Texas Hill Country. However, V2 Landowners concede that

Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmissions Services Corporation’s

(“Applicants”) proposed route, route 894, best meets the criteria set forth in Public Utility

Regulatory Act ("PURA") § 37.056(c) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B). Therefore, the

Administrative Law Judges (“ALJs”) should recommend route 894 to the Public Utility

Commission of Texas (“PUC”) for approval.

        2.       Alternatively, the PUC Staff’s recommended route, route 487, which only slightly

deviates from route 894, also meets the criteria set forth in PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 TAC §

25.101(b)(3)(B), is forward progressing, and constructable. Should the ALJs not recommend route

894, then route 487 should be recommended to the PUC for approval.

                                       II.        BRIEF BACKGROUND

        3.       This matter concerns the Joint Application of Oncor Electric Delivery Company

LLC and LCRA Transmission Service Corporation to amend their Certificates of Convenience

and Necessity for the Bell Court East Switch to Big Hill Substation 765-kV Transmission Line

Project in Bell, Burness, Concho, Coryell, Lampasas, Llano, Mason McCulloch, Menard, Milam,

Mills, San Saba, Schleicher, Tom Green, and Williamson Counties. 1 Applicants filed their joint

application on March 26, 2026. 2

         4.       In the Application, Applicants proposed 122 unique routes. 3 However, Applicants

recognize route 894 as the route that “best meets” the criteria set forth in PURA § 37.056(c) and

16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B). 4

        5.       On May 22, 2026, the PUC Staff filed the direct testimony of John Poole.5 In his

testimony, Mr. Poole recognized route 487 as the route that “best meets” the criteria set forth in

PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B). 6 Mr. Poole did not opine that route 894 did not

meet the criteria set forth in PURA § 37.056(c) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B), only that he

believed that route 487 best met the criteria. 7

        6.       The Hearing on the Merits was held June 8, 2026 to June 12, 2026.

                               III.     ARGUMENTS AND AUTHORITIES

        7.       PURA § 37.056(c)(4) requires consideration of the following factors: (1)

community values; (2) recreational and park areas; (3) historical and aesthetic values; and (4)

environmental integrity, when granting a certificate for a transmission line.

        8.       In addition to the PURA criteria, 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B) requires the

consideration of: (1) whether the routes parallel or utilize existing compatible rights-of-way for

electric facilities; (2) whether the routes parallel or utilize other existing compatible rights-of-way,

including roads, highways, railroads, or telephone rights-of-way; (3) whether the routes parallel

property lines of other natural or cultural features; and (4) whether the routes conform with the

policy of prudent avoidance. Furthermore, 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B) provides that "considering

[the PURA criteria], engineering constraints, and costs, the line must be routed to the extent

a suitable substitute for route 894. 53 Therefore, should the ALJs not recommend route 894, then

route 487 should be recommended to the PUC for approval.

                                              IV.      CONCLUSION

        14.      Understanding that the construction of any 765-kV electric transmission line will

have a profound and negative impact on the Texas Hill Country, V2 Landowners reluctantly

support Applicants’ “best meets” route, route 894. Alternatively, V2 Landowners support the PUC

Staff’s recommended route, route 487, which closely follows route 894, with the exception of

slight deviations.

                                                 V.       PRAYER

        WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, V2 Landowners respectfully request that the

ALJs recommend route 894 to the PUC for approval; alternatively, should the ALJs not

recommend route 894, then route 487 should be recommended to the PUC for approval, and for

such further relief to which Intervenors may be entitled.

        7.       PURA § 37.056(c)(4) requires consideration of the following factors: (1)

community values; (2) recreational and park areas; (3) historical and aesthetic values; and (4)

environmental integrity, when granting a certificate for a transmission line.

        8.       In addition to the PURA criteria, 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B) requires the

consideration of: (1) whether the routes parallel or utilize existing compatible rights-of-way for

electric facilities; (2) whether the routes parallel or utilize other existing compatible rights-of-way,

including roads, highways, railroads, or telephone rights-of-way; (3) whether the routes parallel

property lines of other natural or cultural features; and (4) whether the routes conform with the

policy of prudent avoidance. Furthermore, 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B) provides that "considering

         12.     Because the deviations between route 487 and 894 are minimal, the difference in

park or recreational areas where route 894 has none.51

37.056(c) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B), route 487 only slightly deviates from route 89452 and is

a suitable substitute for route 894.53 Therefore, should the ALJs not recommend route 894, then

route 487 should be recommended to the PUC for approval.
